audit_findings.title: Material unreserved Indian tax claims may sit ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $93.168m of current demands plus a separately disclosed $792m assessment, up to $885.168m combined before additional interest and penalties; $4.74 per diluted share and 12.2% of $7.257bn base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse resolution creates a discrete claim against the equity bridge because historical tax liabilities are not represented by recurring owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: We have appealed all of the outstanding orders from the ITA and have not provided a reserve for the related exposures, which would be material.
audit_findings.explanation: No valuation deduction was made. The June 2026 filing reduced the other demands from $98.093m to $93.168m but confirms that they remain under appeal and that the $792m matter remains before the Supreme Court. The company expects to prevail, so this is not a demonstrated liability; nevertheless, the filed face amounts are large enough to reverse the base conclusion that $38.86 value exceeds the $37.32 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $93.168m demands and $792m assessment for overlap, update accrued interest and penalties, verify deposits or indemnities, obtain current appellate status and legal probability estimates, then rerun the equity bridge under probability-weighted and adverse outcomes.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 cash-flow uplift may include a non-recurring customer advance
audit_findings.magnitude: $170.0m filed advance, equal to 35.4% of the $479.7m owner-earnings anchor; actual anchor contamination unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If owner earnings retained the working-capital inflow, the advance raises the anchor before the associated services and costs are fully incurred, and that elevated anchor is capitalized throughout the DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had received advances of $170.0 million under this arrangement, which contributed to higher cash flows from operating activities in 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the advance increased 2025 operating cash flow, but the supplied record does not show whether the owner-earnings worksheet removed it. Customer advances subsequently declined, and first-half 2026 operating cash flow fell as customer advances unwound. Because the filed advance is more than one-third of the anchor, even partial inclusion could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $170.0m receipt and the related contract-liability movement through every line of the 2025 owner-earnings calculation; remove only the net working-capital benefit not matched by 2025 revenue, service costs or future obligations, and rerun all scenarios if any contamination is demonstrated.

audit_findings.title: India Enforcement Directorate exposure is an unmodeled contingent equity claim
audit_findings.mechanism: A demand, forfeiture, payment or impairment of the liened Gurgaon property would reduce the equity bridge; recurring owner earnings do not capture a historical restructuring claim.
audit_findings.evidence: If the ED issues a demand and ultimately prevails in this matter, it would likely have a material adverse effect on our results of operations and financial condition.
audit_findings.explanation: The February 2026 ED order and property lien are demonstrated, but no demand amount was disclosed. The June 2026 10-Q does not establish that the matter was released, settled or quantified. The company says an adverse outcome would likely be material, but the current record cannot measure the exposure or establish its probability.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the ED order, identify the liened property's carrying and realizable values, confirm whether any demand, provision, deposit, security interest or payment arose through the latest date, obtain counsel's probability assessment, and rerun the bridge for supported outcomes.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter and bridge may omit the XponentL earn-out
audit_findings.magnitude: $77.5m earn-out paid in first-quarter 2026 and therefore already reflected in June 2026 cash; XponentL contributed $21.798m of 2025 revenue, 0.43% of Genpact's $5.079879bn revenue
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid earn-out would reduce the equity bridge, while failure to recognize the acquired business's full-year contribution could understate prospective growth and owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: This amount represents cash consideration of $82.7 million (including $2.3 million of cash acquired) and earn-out consideration of $77.5 million payable by us in March 2026 to the sellers of XponentL.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 filing demonstrates that the full $77.5m earn-out was paid and no amount remained outstanding, so the June 30 cash balance already reflects that payment and there is no demonstrated bridge omission. The separate perimeter issue remains unresolved because the $479.7m anchor contains only a partial year of XponentL, while no acquired-business owner earnings or full-year contribution is supplied. Its reported 2025 revenue contribution was small relative to consolidated revenue, but profitability is unavailable, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Document the March 2026 payment reconciliation to bridge cash and obtain XponentL's monthly revenue, operating profit, working capital and maintenance-capex contribution; then test whether the existing growth scenarios already capture the full-year effect before making any rerun adjustment.

audit_findings.title: Retrospective employee-benefit contributions remain unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Retrospective contributions, interest and penalties for past employee service would be a discrete equity claim rather than an ordinary prospective compensation expense in owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: If applied retrospectively, the interpretation would result in an increase in contributions payable by the Company for past periods for certain of its India-based employees.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 filing repeats that retrospective application could increase past-period contributions but that timing and amount cannot be reliably estimated. This is distinct from the separately recorded $19.055m prior-service cost arising from the 2025 labor codes. The possibility remains open, but the record cannot establish its valuation materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain counsel's latest interpretation, affected employee and payroll-period data, contribution-rate shortfalls, interest and penalty estimates, and any provision or payment after June 2026; rerun the bridge only for an evidence-supported exposure.

audit_findings.title: Only genuinely excess cash should be added to equity value
audit_findings.magnitude: $517.387m added cash, equal to $2.77 per diluted share and 7.1% of $7.257bn base equity value; excluding it would reduce base value from $38.86 to approximately $36.09 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding operating, restricted or earmarked cash as a non-operating asset overstates the equity bridge because such cash is required to support the owner earnings already capitalized.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in short term investments is primarily due to additional investments made in term deposits during 2025 using the proceeds of the 2025 Senior Notes (as defined below).
audit_findings.explanation: The specific $350m debt-funded term deposits matured and the related $350m notes were repaid before June 30, so that historical earmarking does not demonstrate that the remaining cash is debt-funded. However, the valuation adds the entire June cash balance despite the company's disclosed need to fund payroll and administration ahead of receivable collection. Because full exclusion would move base value below the $37.32 market price, the unresolved excess-cash determination is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash by entity and jurisdiction; identify restricted balances, trapped cash and repatriation taxes; calculate minimum operating cash from payroll, seasonal working-capital requirements and liquidity policy; then rerun the bridge using only the evidenced excess portion.
